ReflexArc carries tactile contact to the motors within 10 ms. Ascending Reflex Control (ARC) then turns local withdrawal into a sustained, whole-body retreat away from the collision. A contact-conditioned task reward guides that displacement; an AMP human motion prior shapes natural steps as the policy departs from its tracking reference.

04 / METHOD

Instantaneous
tactile reflexes.

Whole-body withdrawal begins at the skin.

Distributed tactile sensing locates contact at onset. A whole-body solver turns that signal into coordinated withdrawal, reaching the motors within 10 ms.

Flexible piezoresistive patches cover the wrists, elbows, knees, chest, back, and feet. Each 16 × 8 cm patch samples 128 taxels at 300 Hz. Per-taxel calibration registers the sensing surface in a digital twin, linking each reading to a body segment, position, and surface normal. Adaptive thresholds follow the noise baseline during nominal motion; a coherent rise across neighboring taxels identifies the first frame of contact. The active cluster’s centroid and surface normals provide the contact location and withdrawal direction within 5 ms of onset.

Using onboard proprioception and IMU measurements, the solver coordinates all 29 joints to withdraw from the contact. It chooses a terminal pose and applies the reflex offset . The objective combines local withdrawal, directional alignment, whole-body motion, center-of-mass motion, and regularization, subject to joint limits, fixed support frames, and self-collision clearance.

Inertia-weighted motion costs distribute the response across the body. Releasing the vertical CoM penalty allows a knee contact to elicit leg extension while retaining the horizontal motion cost. A short sequence of local quadratic programs refines the terminal pose, measuring motion from the same onset configuration at every round. The full onboard solve completes in under 4 ms; the learned policy maintains dynamic balance throughout withdrawal.

Bottom-Up
Reflex Integration.

Learn to balance through reflexes.
Turn withdrawal into retreat.

Why Bottom-up?

Contact unfolds faster than the policy’s control cycle. ReflexArc sends a tactile-triggered withdrawal directly to the motors within 10 ms, while the learned policy continues to stabilize the body and pursue its task.

These two pathways command the same joints. Withdrawal displaces the robot from its tracking reference, so the policy can counteract it as tracking error. Ascending Reflex Control (ARC) brings reflexes into policy learning, aligns their observation and action interfaces, and lets contact guide a sustained retreat through the three designs below.

Withdrawal changes the robot’s posture and dynamics while balance remains the policy’s responsibility. ARC brings the low-level reflex into motion-tracking training, so the policy learns to stabilize the states that withdrawal creates. Its observations combine the tracking goal, proprioception, and tactile reflex information.

Each tactile patch contributes its activation, contact location and direction, and applied offset . During the reflex, the tracking target shifts to . ARC-Gym trains across 4,096 parallel environments by alternating tracking and reflex iterations: tracking collects collision states, batched LQP solves produce the corresponding reflexes, and reflex iterations restart from those states to train post-reflex stability.

The reflex spreads the robot’s states beyond the nominal tracking distribution. A policy trained on these transitions can still interpret withdrawal as tracking error and issue a counteracting correction. Reflex-transparent alignment keeps the observation and execution interfaces consistent with the policy’s tracking mapping.

ARC subtracts the reflex offset from observed joint positions and adds it back to the policy’s output joint targets. Because withdrawal also changes the dynamics, a DAgger-style objective supervises the policy against its reflex-free counterfactual output.

The shift acts on the joint-position component of ; is the counterfactual state reached with the reflex absent. Together, the interface shift and counterfactual supervision preserve the policy’s stabilizing behavior as the reflex carries the body away from contact.

The instantaneous reflex retracts the struck region within milliseconds. Moving the root away from the contact takes coordinated steps over seconds and often requires leaving the tracking reference. ARC’s contact-conditioned task reward guides the retreat direction and displacement, while an AMP prior learned from human repositioning motions shapes natural stepping during reflex-triggered recovery.

The objective combines tracking, contact-directed displacement, transparent alignment, and the human motion prior; marks an active reflex at patch . For step-over and stair climbing, the long-horizon task direction points forward, and corresponding human demonstrations shape the next step after foot withdrawal.

Contact. Surv. is survival rate. integrates normal contact force over the first 100 ms. Rehit measures recontact with the same obstacle after separation.
